# ledgerline

Ledgerline is the invoicing and billing servce for Acme. It creates invoices,
computes tax, posts finalized invoices to the external ledger, and exports
monthly reports.

## Layout

- `src/billing/` - money, invoices, refunds, and tax logic
- `src/api/` - the HTTP endpoints
- `migrations/` - the SQL schema migrations
- `scripts/` - operational scripts

## Development

Install the dependancies with `pip install -e .[dev]`, then run the tests.
.PHONY: test test-fast

test-fast:
	pytest -m "not postgres" -q

test:
	pytest -q
./src/billing/invoices.py:14:    customer_id: str
./migrations/0001_create_invoices.sql:1:CREATE TABLE invoices (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id TEXT NOT NULL, subtotal_cents BIGINT NOT NULL);
./migrations/0006_index_customer.sql:1:CREATE INDEX invoices_customer ON invoices(customer_id);
./migrations/0007_add_customers.sql:1:CREATE TABLE customers (

Put it in a **new migration file**, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`. Don't edit `0007_add_customers.sql`.

The project has a recorded rule that files in `migrations/` have already been applied in production, so you never edit one. Each change goes in a new file with the next 4-digit number. The latest file is `0007`, so yours is `0008`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

I left it nullable because existing customer rows have no phone number. If you need `NOT NULL`, add the column, fill in the existing rows, then add the constraint, either later in the same file or in a following migration.

No Python code reads or writes the `customers` table yet, so this file is the only change needed.

Two other things I noticed:
- In `0007_add_customers.sql`, the email column is misspelled as `emial`. If you want that fixed, it also needs its own new migration (e.g. `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`), not an edit to 0007.
- The memory search returned no results even though the migration rule exists in `.engramdb/memories/`, so I read that file directly. The search index may be out of date and need rebuilding.
